report.source_text: The patient was followed up once in our service 5 months after the surgery (December 2021). We performed an abdominal ultrasound that showed a surgical triangular scar in the VIIth hepatic segment. The surgical scar appeared to be hyperechoic and had a diameter of 35/21 mm. The liver was inhomogeneous, typical for liver cirrhosis. No hepatic nodules were found on the ultrasound examination. Blood analysis revealed nitrogen retention, the bilirubin levels were slightly increased, a normal platelet count, a normal hemoglobin level and a normal AFP level. The patient was also followed in an oncology service 6 months after the surgery and performed a computed tomography (CT) scan (January 2022) that showed no sign of tumor recurrence.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Hepatocellular carcinoma (G2), pT2 N0 M0 L0 V1 R0, BCLC Stage A
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old woman with autoimmune liver disease and cirrhosis was found to have a 9-10 mm subcapsular hepatic nodule in segments VI/VII on ultrasound in October 2020. MRI in June 2021 showed a hypovascular LI-RADS 3 nodule, with a slight AFP elevation of 10.8 ng/ml. Ultrasound in June 2021 documented nodule growth to 29 mm. Liver biopsy histology and immunohistochemistry in July 2021 confirmed moderately differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma (G2), with pathological staging pT2 Nx Mx L0 V1 R0. Follow-up clinical and imaging data including surgery with no detectable recurrence by December 2021 and January 2022 supported N0 M0 staging and BCLC Stage A classification. The clinical course and pathological findings support the hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis ultimately confirmed by histopathology.
